translation.english_text: Alas—I was deceived. After so many hardships I crossed the sea and came. Kalyani, all morning my hopes surged: I would see you, see my brother-in-law, see Father. Into my heart she poured poison... The deceitful woman, after fondling and flirting with me, has done me cruel harm; she might as well have killed me. A pauper... a wanderer—must I appear before my sister like this? Poverty, theft, deceit, prostitution! Where? In a country where unfailing life-giving rivers flow in abundance, on a land where fertile groves bloom and flourish! People unable to live, people who do not know a way to live, people born only to live! In this land, must every conceivable thing come upon me and torment me? O sacred land of lions! When did you become a spider's web? O prosperous Tamil land that gives life to those who come to you! How long have you been exploiting your own native sons? O my precious golden land, exalted again and again by chronicling the examples of heroic women! Why do you let prostitutes roam your streets and close your eyes? Why? Mansions touching the sky, people who have lost their honour; lofty towers... lowly hearts! O Tamil Nadu! Is this your greatness? Your worth? Your splendour? Kalyani!... you in Madurai... I on the streets of Madras! With a mind overturned and confused... orphaned, without support! Mute, unable to speak to anyone!... Ayyo... Kalyani... Kalyani.

notes: This highly rhetorical monologue is translated for semantic force while retaining its repetitions, apostrophes and contrasts.
The source word `வங்கத்திலே` is semantically anomalous in the Madras/Tamil Nadu setting; the English uses the context-neutral `in this land` and records the issue here rather than altering the Tamil.
The source sequence `தகுதி? போக்கியதை?` is compressed/unclear; `Your worth? Your splendour?` is provisional and remains review-sensitive.
The English page segments preserve the source break `நெஞ்சிலே / நஞ்சைக்` as an intentionally interrupted phrase.
